searchScope: Bounded R2 prescriptive decisions; not systematic review or exhaustive meta-analysis
access: Web literature + official public NCBI BioC; no login/paywall bypass. HTML failures kept visible.

sources.title: The GRONORUN study: is a graded training program for novice runners effective in preventing running related injuries? Design of a Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.authors: Buist I, Bredeweg SW, Lemmink KAPM et al.
sources.read: Methods/design, Study population, Training program and Table 1; publisher text verified 2026-10-24
sources.population: Novice adults preparing for a recreational four-mile event; both sexes; study eligibility not equivalent to app eligibility
sources.finding: Published first week uses ten one-minute runs alternating one-minute walks, three sessions, comfortable speech; five-minute walking warmup/cooldown.
sources.limits: Protocol is exposure provenance, not results or individual safety validation. Does not test concurrent strength progression. Source medical eligibility procedure is not imported as app clearance.
sources.bias: Self-selected event entrants and individual unsupervised execution; no claim of population representativeness

sources.title: No effect of a graded training program on the number of running-related injuries in novice runners: a randomized controlled trial
sources.authors: Buist I, Bredeweg SW, van Mechelen W et al.
sources.read: PubMed abstract read by author. Independent SSCTR reports initial nine-page PDF retrieval followed by deeper-fetch timeout; no exhaustive author/independent full-body verification claim.
sources.population: 532 novice runners preparing for recreational 4-mile event
sources.finding: The graded 13-week schedule did not reduce injury incidence versus standard eight-week schedule.
sources.limits: Not an equivalence/safety trial and not evidence for any universal weekly percentage; no hybrid dosing.

sources.title: Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
sources.read: Search tool returned Methods eligibility, Discussion, sensitivity analyses and Conclusion; direct PMC returned CAPTCHA and publisher 403. Not classified as decisive eligible full-text access by this author.; subsequently read official public NCBI BioC XML: relevant Methods/Discussion/Limitations passages on 2026-10-24
sources.population: Healthy adults; supervised trials >=6 weeks; athletes, clinical groups and explicitly unsupervised RT excluded
sources.finding: Multiple load/set/frequency combinations improve muscle outcomes relative to no exercise; exact comparative equivalence is not established.
sources.limits: Chronic group outcomes do not establish acute one-set adequacy, first-session safety, individual RIR or exact hybrid prescriptions. Overlap with 2026 overview means not independent replication.

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.authors: Currier BS, D'Souza AC, Fiatarone Singh MA et al.
sources.read: Verified PubMed title/authors/date/DOI and indexed excerpts; PMC CAPTCHA and LWW access error recorded; subsequently read official public NCBI BioC XML: relevant Methods/Discussion/Limitations passages on 2026-10-24
sources.population: Healthy adults from novices to experienced; RCT reviews, chronic muscle/physical outcomes
sources.finding: Supports progressive individualized RT; exact RIR targets and total-dose integration retain uncertainty.
sources.limits: An overview does not approve four-machine 1x8, 120-second rest or re-entry week. Chronic evidence cannot prove immediate fatigue removal. Overlaps 2023 review.

sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.read: Methods, Results and Discussion; especially Results 3.2/3.3 and Discussion comparing training status/methods
sources.population: Healthy adults, supervised concurrent >=4 weeks; mixed training status and endurance modes
sources.finding: Pooled maximal-strength and whole-muscle hypertrophy effects were not clearly impaired; explosive-strength attenuation depended partly on session arrangement.
sources.limits: Not proof of no individual interference, or a universal separation threshold. Different endpoints/populations can disagree. Does not quantify one athlete's acute fatigue.
sources.bias: Moderate average trial quality; participant blinding impractical; limited finely stratified training status.

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population: Runners across heterogeneous acute ST protocols, including muscle-damaging and familiar protocols
sources.finding: Acute outcomes vary by protocol and endpoint; pooled submaximal outcomes and individual performance results do not uniformly worsen.
sources.limits: Performance results were not pooled because reporting/timepoints differed. Overlap alone cannot prove necessity or exact set/repetition reduction; no universal recovery-hours rule.
sources.bias: Small heterogeneous protocols; some exercise-induced-damage protocols atypical of routine sessions

sources.title: Monitoring the athlete training response: subjective self-reported measures trump commonly used objective measures: a systematic review
sources.authors: Saw AE, Main LC, Gastin PB
sources.read: Search returned Methods, Results tables and Discussion; direct PMC CAPTCHA
sources.population: Athletes across sports; heterogeneous subjective and objective measures
sources.finding: Well-being self-reports respond to training changes; objective and subjective associations are inconsistent.
sources.limits: No causal recipe or fatigue-score cutoff. RPE during a bout differs from well-being; composite scores can hide subscales.
sources.accessFailure: Official BioC returned429 after PMC CAPTCHA; no retry to evade throttling.

sources.title: Effects of tapering on performance in endurance athletes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.authors: Wang Z, Wang YT, Gao W, Zhong Y
sources.read: Methods eligibility, Results, Discussion and Limitations
sources.population: Well-trained endurance athletes; mostly male; chiefly running/cycling
sources.finding: Reducing pre-event volume while retaining relevant intensity can improve time-trial performance in studied endurance protocols.
sources.limits: Subgroup ranges are not an athlete-specific prescription. Recreational hybrid 10K/half plus Strength week was not directly tested. Does not prove maintenance from one strength session.
sources.bias: Few RCTs, sex/training-status imbalance and heterogeneous tapers

sources.title: The Measurement and Application of Critical Speed and D' in Running: A Scoping Review
sources.authors: Anderson M, Sabapathy S, Arnold B, Bellenger C, Kolodziej F, Bellinger P
sources.population: Running studies with diverse populations, tests and modelling methods; not universal novice calibration
sources.finding: CS, LT2, MLSS and other physiological thresholds are related but non-interchangeable; repeat comparison requires consistent method/context.
sources.limits: No formal statistical comparison or comprehensive risk-of-bias appraisal. Abstract/Results counts inconsistent, so counts not propagated. Does not validate HR-derived or device power defaults.

sources.title: Steady-state VO2 above MLSS: evidence that critical speed better represents maximal metabolic steady state in well-trained runners
sources.read: Indexed Discussion, no direct access claimed
sources.finding: Different metabolic measurements can locate different speeds within the same athletes.
sources.limits: Small specific measurement sample; does not justify universal numeric conversion from CS to MLSS.

sources.title: Trainability of repetitions-in-reserve estimation in younger and older adults: a parallel-group repeated-measures study
sources.population: 26 recreationally active adults, 13 younger and 13 older, prior RT but no RIR regulation experience; supervised bench/leg press
sources.finding: RIR estimates improved with practice but remained task/target dependent and imperfect.
sources.limits: Study repeatedly trained to failure under supervision; do not copy that familiarization into V1. Not proof exact RIR safe/known in novice or other exercises.
sources.bias: Small nonrandom age groups; no pure untrained RT group; task-specific transfer uncertain

sources.title: Cardiorespiratory and metabolic consequences of detraining in endurance athletes
sources.authors: Barbieri A, Fuk A, Gallo G, Gotti D, Meloni A, La Torre A, Filipas L, Codella R
sources.read: Indexed abstract/discussion; direct open CAPTCHA; subsequently read official public NCBI BioC XML: relevant Methods/Discussion/Limitations passages on 2026-10-24
sources.population: Endurance athletes; heterogeneous short/long cessation and prior status
sources.finding: Training cessation can alter capacities at different rates; previous tolerance is not present capacity.
sources.limits: No validated return recipe or universal duration/percentage; relevant full-text sections read via official BioC after HTML access failure.

sources.title: Comparison of muscle hypertrophy following 6-month of continuous and periodic strength training
sources.authors: Ogasawara R, Yasuda T, Ishii N, Abe T
sources.population: 14 young men, bench-press-only periodic versus continuous training
sources.finding: Periodic retraining outcomes can recover over repeated cycles in a small specific study.
sources.limits: Does not approve post-pause full-body loads, older adults, hybrid training or a first-return percentage.

sources.title: Maintaining Physical Performance: The Minimal Dose of Exercise Needed to Preserve Endurance and Strength Over Time
sources.authors: Spiering BA, Mujika I, Sharp MA, Foulis SA
sources.read: PubMed abstract and indexed publisher Reduced Frequency/Volume; direct LWW open failed
sources.population: Predominantly general populations; limited athlete-specific evidence
sources.finding: Some chronic outcomes persist with reduced frequency/volume when intensity is retained.
sources.limits: Narrative/indirect. Not proof that 1x5 preserves all strength qualities or is optimal during hybrid race week.
